title: POC scoping - Private networking & data residency (Equinex Health)
summary: Equinex Health wants a 4-week POC to validate Redwood Private in their AWS VPC with strict egress controls and EU/US data residency. Success criteria: sub-100ms median token latency for 512-token chat workload, cost per 1k tokens within projected budget, and SOC2-level audit logs visible to Equinex. Action items include network diagram, benchmark plan, and a security questionnaire. Next milestone: kick-off lab and test run on 2026-07-20.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, and with me is Priya from our SE team. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Marta Ruiz: Marta here, CTO at Equinex. Devon, Alyssa, Benji are on too.
[00:13] Devon Chen: here.
[00:15] Alyssa Park: hi, thanks.
[00:17] Jordan Lee: Great; agenda — scope the POC: networking model (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), regions/data residency, workload sizing for our benchmarks, and success criteria + timeline.
[00:29] Priya Natarajan: I'll walk through the technical constraints then we can map them to the POC tasks.
[00:33] Marta Ruiz: goal is to verify Redwood Private in our AWS environment with no public egress, everything must stay in our VPCs or via approved endpoints. Also need logs for audits.
[00:44] Jordan Lee: Understood. High level — Redwood Private supports both VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink. Peering is straightforward, lower latency but needs cross-account peering and route table changes; PrivateLink provides interface endpoints and tighter control, sometimes preferred for compliance.
[01:05] Devon Chen: Our infra team prefers PrivateLink because we can restrict the ENIs and keep tighter egress controls. But there's some cost tradeoffs and region support concerns.
[01:15] Priya Natarajan: Right — for the POC we can prototype both if you'd like, but most customers pick one for production. For benchmarks, we need to size the baseline workload: what QPS, average prompt length, and concurrency do you expect?
[01:31] Marta Ruiz: For initial tests: chat assistant used by clinicians. Typical prompt around 250-400 tokens, but we want to test 512 tokens for worst-case. Concurrent sessions about 40 peak users, likely ~20 simultaneous inference streams. Target is 50 requests per second during peak stress test.
[01:47] Benji O'Neal: Also want embeddings pipeline — batch of 10k documents overnight, but that's less latency sensitive. Focus POC on chat latency and throughput.
[01:57] Priya Natarajan: Good. For 512-token sequences and 20 parallel streams, we'll recommend an instance profile (GPU type + replicas) for the POC; we'll give a cost estimate. For latency targets, you mentioned sub-100ms median per token?
[02:12] Marta Ruiz: Sub-100ms median token latency or under 250ms per response for typical prompts, whichever is realistic. Ultimately clinicians can't wait more than a couple hundred millis for a reply.
[02:23] Jordan Lee: We can craft a benchmark plan: synthetic replay of your traffic (prompt distribution you provide), then run steady-state and spike tests. Success criteria we propose: median token latency <100ms for 512 tokens, 95th percentile response time <600ms, no errors above 0.5% during a 30-minute steady test, and cost per 1k tokens under your budget threshold — we'll leave the budget threshold to you to define.
[02:47] Alyssa Park: On security: SOC2, SAML SSO integration, RBAC, KMS for key management, and audit logs are must-haves. Also need data residency in US-East for PHI and EU-West for EU patients.
[03:03] Priya Natarajan: Redwood Private supports customer KMS and can integrate with your KMS/HSM for key wrapping. Audit logs are emitted to a customer S3 or to your SIEM via secured forwarder. For SSO we do SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
[03:19] Devon Chen: Any limitations around cross-region endpoints? We have multi-region VPCs and prefer dedicated endpoints in each region to avoid cross-region egress.
[03:28] Jordan Lee: We can deploy private instances in multiple regions; you'll need a dedicated cluster per region if strict residency required. For the POC we can stand up a US-East cluster and an EU-West test cluster if you want to validate residency. There is some overhead but it's standard.
[03:47] Benji O'Neal: Egress — we block all outbound except to approved endpoints. Will Redwood require outbound to external addresses?
[03:56] Priya Natarajan: With PrivateLink, all traffic stays on AWS network and terminates at our service interface. No public egress is required. If you choose peering, traffic stays within VPC peering routes — also no NAT egress needed. The only external calls would be for telemetry if you enable it; but we can disable telemetry or route it to your collectors.
[04:18] Marta Ruiz: Good. For PII handling: can you guarantee model inputs aren't used for training?
[04:24] Jordan Lee: Redwood's enterprise commitments include no training on customer data for provided Private deployments; we'll include contractual language.
[04:31] Devon Chen: Ok. Next — benchmark plan details?
[04:35] Priya Natarajan: We'll need sample traffic: a small dataset of prompts (anonymized) and expected request distribution. We'll produce a benchmark harness that replays traffic to the private endpoint. For instrumentation we'll push traces to your X-Ray/Datadog if you want, otherwise we'll provide our own telemetry to review with you.
[04:54] Alyssa Park: For logs retention — we need 12 months of audit logs and ability to export them to our S3. Also need proof of encryption at rest.
[05:03] Jordan Lee: We can configure audit export to your S3 and confirm SSE-KMS. We'll send the security architecture doc.
[05:11] Marta Ruiz: Timeline — we want to run the POC in 4 weeks, ideally starting the week of July 20. That gives us time to review network details and sign an MOU. Is that feasible?
[05:21] Priya Natarajan: Yes — typical POC: week 0 network + infra setup, week 1 benchmark setup + small smoke tests, week 2 steady-state and spike tests, week 3 tuning and final report. So starting 2026-07-20 lines up.
[05:34] Benji O'Neal: Network operations will need a diagram and a small terraform snippet for the PrivateLink interface VPC endpoint.
[05:40] Jordan Lee: We'll supply a network diagram and a Terraform module for the PrivateLink endpoint and peering options.
[05:46] Devon Chen: Cost estimation during POC — how do we track token usage?
[05:50] Jordan Lee: Our console can show token-level breakdowns by route and model; for Private we can forward usage metrics to your billing account or provide CSV exports. We'll send estimated GPU-hours and token costs for the proposed config.
[06:03] Alyssa Park: Any known performance regressions with quantized models? We use quantized 4-bit for cost reasons, is that supported?
[06:11] Priya Natarajan: Yes, Redwood supports quantized execution paths and we can test both FP16 and 4-bit quantized variants. We'll include quality regression checks in the POC — BLEU/ROUGE aren't relevant for chat but we'll do human eval sampling and automatic metrics on a held-out prompt set.
[06:30] Marta Ruiz: Success criteria recap: median token latency <100ms for 512 tokens, 95th percentile <600ms, error rate <0.5%, embeddings throughput for overnight job completes under target window, audit logs exported and encrypted, and no public egress.
[06:47] Jordan Lee: That matches what we propose. Any blockers on your side?
[06:51] Devon Chen: We need security sign-off and a thin MOU. Also coordination window for our network team — they only have a 2-hour slot next Monday.
[06:59] Jordan Lee: We'll work around that. We'll send the network diagram and the Terraform snippet ahead of the slot.
[07:06] Benji O'Neal: One more question — can we run benchmarks on our synthetic data with the KV cache warm? We want to evaluate cold vs warm latency.
[07:15] Priya Natarajan: Absolutely — we'll do cold-start and warm cache runs. We'll also capture KV cache hit rates. Note sometimes transcript systems misread KV as "K V cash" — small transcription joke.
[07:27] Marta Ruiz: ha, noted.
[07:30] Jordan Lee: Next steps: we'll outline the POC plan and deliverables. Priya, do you want to speak to the benchmark artifacts you'll deliver?
[07:36] Priya Natarajan: Sure — deliverables: 1) network diagram + terraform snippets for PrivateLink and peering options, 2) benchmark harness and replay config (you provide sample prompts), 3) suggested instance types and cost estimate, 4) security architecture doc and SAML/KMS integration checklist, 5) final POC report with latency/cost charts and recommended config.
[07:58] Alyssa Park: We'll share anonymized prompts and the security questionnaire by EOD Friday.
[08:03] Jordan Lee: Great. Any competitors you're evaluating?
[08:06] Marta Ruiz: We're looking at Anthropic and a self-hosted Llama2 variant for certain teams; Google Vertex for managed endpoints is on the shortlist too.
[08:14] Jordan Lee: Noted. We'll highlight diffs in the POC report.
[08:18] Devon Chen: One operational ask — can we restrict updates/rollouts to a canary and not auto-upgrade a model in production?
[08:25] Priya Natarajan: Yes, rollout controls are available — canary, A/B, and pinned model versions for production.
[08:31] Benji O'Neal: For the embeddings overnight job, we might need burst capacity. Can Redwood Dedicated burst from a reserved pool?
[08:39] Jordan Lee: For Dedicated we offer burst options; for Private deployments on your infra we can configure extra workers or schedule batch windows. We'll detail options.
[08:49] Marta Ruiz: Ok, let's recap action items and next steps before we close.
[08:54] Jordan Lee: Sure.
[08:56] Jordan Lee: Action items recap — Jordan to send network diagram & Terraform by 2026-07-13; Priya to send benchmark harness + instance recommendations by 2026-07-13; Equinex to share anonymized prompts and security questionnaire by 2026-07-17; schedule POC kickoff week of 2026-07-20; set network team slot w/ Devon.
[09:16] Devon Chen: We'll confirm the 2-hour window for Monday and Slack you the time.
[09:20] Alyssa Park: We'll also review the contract language for training-on-data and sign the MOU.
[09:25] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Anything else?
[09:27] Marta Ruiz: No, thanks. Looking forward.
[09:29] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with docs and calendar invites.
[09:33] -- call ends --
next_steps: Jordan to send network diagram and Terraform snippets for PrivateLink and peering by 2026-07-13
Priya to provide benchmark harness, replay config, and instance recommendations by 2026-07-13
Equinex to share anonymized prompts and completed security questionnaire by 2026-07-17
Schedule POC kickoff for week of 2026-07-20 (target 2026-07-20)
Devon to confirm 2-hour network ops slot next Monday via Slack
